title: "!! evaluates the argument where {{ }} passes it on as is"

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

mean_of <- function(df, col) {
  summarise(df, m = mean(!!col))
}
x <- 100
measures <- data.frame(x = 1:3)
mean_of(measures, x)
```
:::

## Why

`!!col` injects the **value** of `col`. To get it, R evaluates the argument where the function was called, as for any argument. The `x` of the call then refers to the global variable `x`, which is 100, and not to the column. Without a variable `x` in the environment, you would get an `object 'x' not found` error, which is easier to spot.

`{{ col }}` does something else: it captures the expression `x` without evaluating it, together with its environment, and passes it on to `summarise()`, which looks it up first among the columns. That is almost always what you want from a column argument.

## The fix

Use `{{ }}` to pass an argument on, and keep `!!` for expressions that are already captured, such as the result of `enquo()`.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

mean_of <- function(df, col) {
  summarise(df, m = mean({{ col }}))
}
mean_of(measures, x)

mean_of_enquo <- function(df, col) {
  col <- enquo(col)
  summarise(df, m = mean(!!col))
}
mean_of_enquo(measures, x)
```
:::
